change_since_0_2_0: On 0.2.0 the generated unsigned Uninstall.exe was blocked before process start by Windows Smart App Control (event 3077, 2026-08-27T19:51:26+01:00) and the uninstall stage could not be observed. On this 0.3.0 run the same unsigned uninstaller ran and the full lifecycle passed. The earlier block is recorded rather than deleted: it was a real machine-policy outcome, it was not reproduced here, and an unsigned artefact remains liable to it on any machine whose policy is stricter than this one.

blocker.statement: The release candidate, the frozen application and the generated uninstaller are all unsigned. A public Windows release must be signed: an unsigned setup shows an unknown-publisher warning and can be blocked outright by Smart App Control or enterprise code-integrity policy, as it was on the 0.2.0 run. The lifecycle is now proven on 0.3.0 bytes; the signature is not.

required_to_close: Provide an authorised Authenticode certificate thumbprint, SignTool path and HTTPS RFC 3161 timestamp URL.
Rebuild the frozen application, generated uninstaller and setup through the signed build route.
Re-run the full active install, upgrade and uninstall verifier on the signed release installer.
Reseal the technical trace and record the signed release installer SHA-256.
